en: The Forty-Two Character Contemplation Gate from the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*,
by Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu Qing.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—Grand Master of the Three Great Wisdoms, posthumously titled Grand Preceptor, conferred the purple robe and the rank of Minister of Works, Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households, and granted the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror)—by imperial decree. At that time, the youth Sudhana descended from the celestial palace.
He headed toward the city of Kapilavastu and,
having arrived at the place where the youth Viśvantara was,
prostrated himself with his head at the youth's feet and stood to one side.
He addressed him, saying: "O Noble One,
I have already resolved my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva practice."
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will explain it to me."
Then that youth said to Sudhana,
"Noble son, I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Skillfully Knowing All Arts.'"
I constantly recite and uphold these syllables that are the root of this liberation.

When pronouncing the syllable *Ā* (the letter Ā with the *u* vowel marker), one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called the "Non-differentiated Realm" through the majestic power of the Bodhisattva.
Because one realizes that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
At the time of the syllable *ra*,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of infinite differentiation.
Because one awakens to all phenomena as being free from dust and defilement.
At the time of the syllable BA,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gateway called "The Limit of the Dharmadhātu."
Because one realizes that all phenomena are unattainable in terms of the ultimate truth (paramārthasatya).
When pronouncing the syllable *ka* (left) with a light tone, one enters the gate of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) called "The Universal Wheel that Severs Differentiation."
Because one realizes that all phenomena are devoid of conditioned formations.
When pronouncing the syllable *na* with the tongue-tip,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gate called "The Limit of the Non-existence of Ālayavijñāna."
Because one realizes that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are unattainable.
At the time of the syllable *la*,
one enters the gate of the stainless Prajñāpāramitā.
Because one realizes that all phenomena transcend the world,
and because the causal conditions of the limb of craving never again appear—
at the time of the syllable NA.
They enter the gateway of the practice of the perfection of wisdom of non-retrogression,
because they realize that all phenomena are tamed, tranquil, true thusness, equal, and without discrimination.
At the time of the syllable *ma*,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā called the Vajra-field, realizing that all phenomena are free from bondage and liberation.
At the time of the syllable *ṇa* (with the high tone),...
One enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Universal Wheel,
because one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are free from feverish distress and corruption, thereby attaining cool refreshment.
When pronouncing the syllable *Śrī*:
Entering the ocean-treasury gate of the *prajñāpāramitā*, because one realizes that all phenomena are without obstruction. [The syllable] VAḤ.
At the time of the syllable VAḤ.
Entering the gate of the perfection of wisdom that dwells in universal arising;
because one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are cut off from the path of language.
[The syllable] *ta* (upper tone). When this syllable is uttered:
Entering the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā that illuminates and purifies defilements,
because one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are the immovable True Suchness (tathatā).
At the moment of the syllable YA.
Upon pronouncing the syllable *ṢṬHA*, one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the accumulation of distinctions,
because of awakening to the fact that all phenomena are, in reality, unarisen.
They enter the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of universal radiance that extinguishes feverish affliction,
because they realize that the characteristics of all dharmas— whether as objects to be subdued or as bases to be maintained— are unapprehendable.
When the syllable KA is pronounced,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of diverse categories,
because one realizes that an agent of all phenomena cannot be found.
When pronouncing the syllable *SA*,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Manifesting the Pouring Down of Great Rain," because at the moment of awakening to all phenomena,
their sameness is found to be ungraspable.
When pronouncing the syllable *maṅ* (莽),
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the Great Swift Multitude of Peaks;
one awakens to the fact that the nature of grasping at all phenomena as "mine" is unattainable.
At the time of the syllable Ga,
one enters the gate of the universal wheel that nurtures the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā),
because one realizes that the nature of grasping at the activity of all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the letter *ṭha*,
one enters the gate of the non-differentiated Prajñāpāramitā of True Suchness (*tathatā*),
because one realizes that the locus of all phenomena is unattainable.
At the time of the syllable *ja*,
there is the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of pure ultimate source that enters the worldly cycle of existence;
for one realizes that the arising of all phenomena— both subject and object— is unapprehendable.
At the time of the syllable *Svaḥ*,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Recollection of the Adornments of All Buddhas," because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena is peaceful and ungraspable.
At the time of the syllable *Dha*,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Dharma-realm Samādhi-maṇḍala;
one awakens to the fact that all dharmas cannot be apprehended as having a nature that sustains a realm.
At the time of the syllable ŚA,
one enters the gate of prajñāpāramitā that accords with all Buddha-teachings,
because one realizes that the quiescent nature of all phenomena is ungraspable.
When pronouncing the syllable Kha, one enters the Prajñāpāramitā door of the treasury of wisdom that manifests within the ground of practice;
for one realizes that all phenomena, like the nature of space, are ungraspable.
When pronouncing the syllable *kṣa*,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā door of the ocean-treasury of karma that pacifies through definitive discernment,
because one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are ultimately unattainable in their exhausted nature.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṢṬĀ*,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of pure light that destroys all afflictions;

for one awakens to the fact that the locus where all phenomena abide— whether in what is appropriate or inappropriate— is such that their nature cannot be apprehended as something subject to movement or change.
When pronouncing the syllable *nāṃ* with a light, rising tone,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gate of discerning the world of birth;
this is because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena— both the subject that knows and the object known— is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable RAṬHA,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the Wisdom Maṇḍala that reverses the wheel of birth and death,
because one realizes that the nature of attachment to all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable *VA*,
one enters the gateway of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) that adorns all palaces and sites of enlightenment (*maṇḍala*),
because one realizes that the destructible nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable CA,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā called the Distinctive Path of the Concealing Cover of the Preparatory Application for Cultivation;
this is because one realizes that the nature of desire and delight which conceals all phenomena is unattainable.
At the time of the syllable *sma*,
one enters the gate of the revolving Prajñāpāramitā that manifests the direct perception of all Buddhas of the ten directions;
this is because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena as objects of recollection is unattainable.
When the syllable *Hvaḥ* is uttered,
one enters the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* called "The Universal Birth of the Ocean-Treasury of the Power Capable of Observing All Sentient Beings."
Because one realizes that all phenomena are ungraspable as having a nature that can be summoned.
When pronouncing the syllable *Tsa*,
one enters the gate of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) which is the source and foundation of practice, entering the ocean of all meritorious qualities.
Because one realizes that the courageous and heroic nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable *ga*,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā door of the firm oceanic treasury that sustains the clouds of all phenomena.
Because one realizes that the profound equality of all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable *Ḍha*,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā of making vows to go before and behold all Buddhas appearing in the ten directions.
Because one realizes that the accumulated nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṅa*,
one enters the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of ten million syllables within the accumulation of the wheel of syllables.
Because one realizes that all phenomena are free from all clamor and contention, and because going, coming, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down cannot be apprehended.
At the time of the syllable PHAḤ,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gate of proceeding to the site of enlightenment at the limit of maturing all sentient beings.
Because one realizes that the retribution for the pervasiveness of all phenomena is unattainable.
At the moment of pronouncing the syllable *Ska*,
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā gate called "The Universal Illumination of the Light-Wheel of the Ground-Treasury of Non-Attachment and Unobstructed Liberation."
Because one realizes that the nature of the accumulation of all phenomena as aggregates is unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable *yaṣa*,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā that proclaims the realm of all Buddha-dharmas.
Because one awakens to the fact that the nature and characteristics of senescence in all phenomena are unattainable.
When pronouncing the second syllable of the compound *Śi*,
one enters the gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Universal Illumination by the Thunderous Roar of the Dharma-Cloud Pervading All Space."
Because one realizes that the traces of the accumulation of all phenomena are unattainable.
When pronouncing the syllable ṬHA (upper tone),
one enters the Prajñāpāramitā door of the ultimate limit of benefiting sentient beings through selflessness.
Because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena is characterized by mutual exclusion and is ultimately unapprehendable.
[The syllable] *Ṭa*: at the moment of pronouncing this syllable, one enters the Prajñāpāramitā door of the treasury of the non-differentiation of the Dharma-wheel.
Because one realizes that the ultimate locus of all phenomena is unattainable.
Son of good family, when I pronounce these fundamental syllables for entering the various liberations,
these forty-two [syllables] begin with Prajñāpāramitā.
One enters immeasurable and innumerable gateways of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Furthermore, noble son, this gateway of letters is that by which one can awaken to and enter the ultimate limit of the emptiness of phenomena (*dharmas*).
Excluding such words,
they signify that all phenomena are empty and can no longer be apprehended.
Why is this? Because the meaning of such words cannot be proclaimed,
cannot be demonstrated,
and cannot be grasped.
It cannot be written down or maintained;
it cannot be observed,
for it is free from all marks.
Good son, for example, just as space is the destination to which all things return,
so too are these gateways of letters;
the meaning of the emptiness of all phenomena enters into these gateways.
Only then can it be clearly manifested.
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva attains skillful wisdom regarding such entry into the gates of all syllables,
[they shall realize this].
Regarding all sounds and words, both what they express and what they signify,
he is entirely without obstruction;
and regarding the universal emptiness that is equal in all phenomena.
They are able to realize and maintain them all,
attaining skillfulness in all vocal expressions.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva...
One who is able to hear and thus enter these gateways of syllables,
which are sealed by the syllable A, shall,
upon hearing them, receive and uphold them.
By reciting and mastering [the teachings] and explaining them to others without craving for fame or profit,
one attains twenty kinds of extraordinary merit through these causes and conditions.
What are the twenty? They are:
attaining powerful mindfulness and attaining superior shame and remorse.
One attains firm strength,
attains the essential purport of the Dharma,
and attains superior awakening.
They attain sublime wisdom,
they attain unimpeded eloquence,
and they attain the gateways of dhāraṇī.
One attains freedom from doubt;
one attains the state where neither anger nor attachment arises toward words that are disagreeable or agreeable;
and one attains dwelling in equanimity, free from high and low.
They attain skillfulness regarding the speech and sounds of sentient beings;
they attain skillfulness regarding the aggregates (*skandha*), skillfulness regarding the bases (*āyatana*), and skillfulness regarding the elements (*dhātu*);

they attain skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), skillfulness regarding causes (*hetu*), skillfulness regarding conditions (*pratyaya*), and skillfulness regarding phenomena (*dharma*).
He attains skill in the knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of the faculties, skill in the knowledge of others' minds,
skill in the observation of astrology and calendrics,
skill in the knowledge of the divine ear, skill in the knowledge of recollecting past lives, skill in the knowledge of supernormal powers, and skill in the knowledge of death and rebirth.
They attain skill in the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows;
they attain skill in the knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible;
and they attain skill in the modes of deportment such as coming and going.
This constitutes the attainment of twenty kinds of sublime merits.
Good son, I know only this wisdom of the fundamental syllables that enters all liberations;
as for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, [they are beyond my knowledge].
They are able to penetrate all the skillful dharmas of the world with wisdom and reach the further shore.
"How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of Viśvāmitra.
They circumambulated him countless times, gazing up at him with longing as they departed.
